parsedate: find day names, months and time zones faster

Implements faster lookups for which specific week name, month name and
time zone that is provided; without loops.

Short-cut Alpha and compact the single-letter time-zone table by omitting
the rejected J slot and adjusting the index for later letters.

With this applied, the dateparser perf test completes almost twice as
fast for me.

Add unit test 4781 to verify each parser.

Closes #22981

parsedate: time zone strings

The three and four letter versions are now stored as uint32 to use less
memory and get found slightly faster.

Short-circuit the common Yankee and Zulu timezones and compact the
single-letter table accordingly.

Closes #23000

coupling: The first edited commit short-circuits Alpha and removes Alpha/J from the 26-entry single-letter table while preserving a corrected index calculation. The second edited commit independently short-circuits Yankee/Zulu and removes those two entries while preserving direct letter-index lookup. Each change is safe against its real parent: the first leaves 24 in-range entries and adjusts indices, while the second leaves 24 in-range entries with X as the largest non-short-circuited direct index. Their composition removes four entries but the later direct lookup still maps W to index 22 and X to index 23 in the resulting 22-entry table. A correct repair must restore the table/index invariant across both compactions rather than treating either optimization in isolation.
